highlights.description: Observed runs: pidl generate --observation shows a real system's run beside the walkthrough's examples, each step with the request it sent, the response it got and the tokens it carried, and the exchanges the protocol does not describe
Two new formats: pidl-observation/v1 records what a run exchanged and pidl-binding/v1 describes one deployment's participants, hosts and paths, each with a JSON Schema generated from the Go types

Protocol-agnostic matching: documents say how a step is recognized (match) and where a token travels (carried_in); pidl splits a capture into scenario instances and aligns its exchanges to their steps
The viewer's Concept / Observed switch shows either the document's examples or the run's exchanges, with timing, match strength and the extra exchanges between steps

added.description: The pidl-observation/v1 and pidl-binding/v1 formats, with generated and embedded schemas
Observation and binding schemas generated from the Go types and embedded as schema constants
A flow's match rule: method, path template or pattern, status, headers, body JSON pointers, repeat and optional
Binding step rules keyed by scenario and expanded step ID, by defining scenario and flow ID, or by flow ID alone
observe/match classifies steps as requests, responses, standalone or unobservable, resolves their rules and scores exchanges against them
Body predicates by JSON pointer in match rules
Alignment of a capture's exchanges to a scenario instance's steps, with strong and weak matches, repeated steps and extra exchanges
Splitting a capture into scenario instances, ranked by the steps they explain, within an optional time window
A token definition's carried_in says where the token travels: a header and parameter, or a body JSON pointer, optionally narrowed by JWT typ
Observed runs in the walkthrough format: observed_run and observed_extra on a scenario; observed, observed_status and observed_strength on a step
The walkthrough renderer's Build method and Transform field, so a walkthrough can be changed before it is written

Package observe adds observed entries after their base scenario, decodes the tokens each exchange carries without verifying them, and masks raw token, signature and credential values unless asked not to
pidl generate --observation, --binding, --scenarios, --from, --to and --raw; pidl observe import --from sandbox reads the aauth-go sandbox trace
observe/adapter/sandbox reads the aauth-go sandbox trace as an observation
The viewer's Concept / Observed switch, with each exchange's time and gap, match strength, notes from the capturing tool, and extra exchanges drawn between the steps they followed
Carried tokens are told apart by JWT typ, and a response step pairs with the nearest earlier request going the other way, so a response can follow other steps

highlights.description: Embeddable viewer: @grokify/pidl-viewer shows any walkthrough from a CDN with one script tag, by inline JSON, a URL or ?src=, isolated from the page's styles

Postman collections: pidl generate -f postman writes a runnable collection with values chained between requests, checks on every response, signed requests sent through a signing proxy, and environments per target

added.description: Scenario groups, variants and step IDs: groups order sections, variants follow their base, and flows carry IDs addressed as <include>.<id> inside fragments, for deep links

A curl command for every example request, with a defined wire form for example bodies; signed requests note that their signature headers are replayed

Code samples on flow examples and scenarios: inline code or a region between pidl:begin and pidl:end markers in a repository file; pidl samples resolve writes a lock file and pidl samples check fails on drift
A step with no HTTP message, such as a person approving in a browser, can carry code samples alone
Built-in examples apply their sample lock when loaded, so generating from an example name includes its code

Sample sets (pidl-samples/v1): code samples an implementation keeps apart from the protocol document, each attached to a step by its address, resolved into the set itself and joined with Protocol.WithSampleSet

pidl samples resolve and check accept a sample set; --repo-dir reads every source from one checkout and --protocol checks every step address; generate --samples can be repeated and takes a lock or a sample set
schema/samples.schema.json generated from pidl.SampleSet and embedded as schema.SampleSetSchemaJSON
Viewer tabs for HTTP, cURL and each sample language, remembered across steps, with highlighting and a copy button
postman and postman-environment output formats: a folder per scenario, chained values, checks against each example, polling for deferred responses, mock mode and environments per target

--signer proxy sends requests with HTTP message signatures through a signing proxy: Signature, Signature-Input and Content-Digest are left for the proxy, and Signature-Key names only the scheme and, for jwt, the chained token to present; unsigned requests are sent directly
Postman chaining captures string parameters of response headers: parameters of structured fields, and auth-params of challenges such as the scope of a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge
ResolveOptions.FS resolves the documents that extends and imports name from an fs.FS; built-in examples that extend others are resolved when loaded
Walkthroughs carry "format": "pidl-walkthrough/v1"; the viewer reads any v1 walkthrough and refuses another major version
